title: Colombian police storm supermarket to free 20 held hostage for 17 hours
html:
Relatives of those being held hostage spent anxious hours as the situation unfolded

  • Published

Colombian security forces have freed around 20 shoppers and employees who had been held hostage for about 17 hours at a supermarket in the city of Cartagena.

Gunmen had stormed into the building at 08:00 (13:00 GMT) on Tuesday after what local media said was a failed attempt of robbing an armoured car carrying money and valuables.

They held those inside at gunpoint while trying to negotiate their getaway.

With the situation becoming ever more intense as the day progressed, Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella gave the green light for special forces and police to launch a daring operation to free the hostages, in which one gunman was killed.

Around 20 people were still being held hostage when the security forces moved in

Residents living near the supermarket reported hearing explosions as the security forces moved into the building.

Police later confirmed that officers had used stun grenades to overpower the hostage takers.

De la Espriella described it as "an extraordinary joint operation", which he said had been carried out "flawlessly".

He flew into the northern city to oversee the operation.

In footage released since then, he can be seen speaking into a walkie-talkie and carrying a handgun strapped to his side.

Speaking after the successful rescue of the hostages, he said that the gunmen had been given the chance to hand themselves in, which they had refused.

Earlier in the day, the men had freed 10 of their hostages, among them elderly women.

But they continued to hold around 20, even as a police helicopter hovered above and special forces erected a perimeter around the building.

Local media said that as well as demanding safe passage out of the supermarket, the gunmen also demanded nearly $2m (£1.5m) and armoured vehicles.

According to President De la Espriella, they had no political affiliations but had taken the hostages once their plan to rob an armoured car carrying money had been foiled.

"It's not that a terrorist group carried out a kidnapping - no, these are criminals who were caught off guard, had no way out, and then kidnapped a group of people," he said.

Photos taken during the rescue operation show armed soldiers inside the building while people are kneeling with their hands behind their heads.
summary: One gunman was killed in the operation to free around 20 shoppers and employees after a 17-hour hostage ordeal.
